resolutions.title: A second apostrophe closes the first one's quote, so a non-orbit line can still hide an orbit line

options_presented.label: A
options_presented.body: In extractFenceLines, when a join began on a line whose first token is not the tool, fail extraction for each joined line whose first token is the tool, naming its own line. Add the two-apostrophe injection.

options_presented.label: B
options_presented.body: Narrow the quoted-argument row's last clause to a quote still open at the fence's end, and add to the places limit's residual kind: an orbit line inside a quote another line opens and a later line closes.

resolutions.action: Applied the ratified direction A: when a join began on a line whose first token is not the tool, each joined line whose first token is the tool fails extraction at its own line ('inside a quote opened at line N by another command'), so the row's clause — a line of another tool cannot hide the orbit lines after it — now holds. Tests: the two-apostrophe case in the places table and an injection into a real reference fence; both fail against the previous helper. The surface still sweeps clean. The spec row and design D3 state the rule.

introduced.text: fails extraction at its own line, though a later line closes the quote
a quote a later line closes fails extraction at the held orbit line

resolutions.title: A trailing backslash on a command that takes a positional passes silently, not as a false failure
resolutions.action: The trailing-backslash residual names both outcomes: a false failure on a command that takes no positional, and on one that does (orbit validate), a parse that passes while the continued flags go unchecked.

retired: as an argument, a false failure)

introduced.text: a parse that passes while the continued flags go unchecked

final_assessment: Two of two resolved: Sal took A, so an orbit line held inside another command's quote now fails at its own line, and the continuation residual names its silent outcome.
